findings:
🟡 [watch-project-identity-not-normalized] MUST-FIX `src/status/runs-watch.js:resolveKey` returns null for a full `repo_identity` argument, so `status runs --watch|--stop --project git-common-dir:/…` exits 2 with "--project must be a 16-hex project key", and `runs-fields.js:applySelectors` echoes the raw selector as `project` instead of the normalized key; §2.7 (binding) says `--project` accepts the 16-hex key or the full `repo_identity` string and the CLI normalizes to `project_key`. Impact: the documented identity form is rejected on the watcher/stop path and the JSON header is not normalized. Smallest fix: in `resolveKey`, when `projectArg` is not 16-hex but starts with `git-common-dir:` return `projectKey(projectArg)` (watchLaunchArgv/isWatcherFor then see the normalized key, so `--stop` keeps matching); in `applySelectors` set `result.project_key` to the normalized key (keep `project` for compatibility).
🔵 [fresh-bound-candidate-set] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `freshBoundOf` counts only this project's post-selector rows while `buildRunRows` rotates over every live run in the shared manifest dir; with several projects live, a row can age past the bound and drop to `unknown` (conservative, never falsely confirmed), mitigated by the shared cursor interleaving. Excluded: spec direction preserved (unknown, not running); follow-up is to derive candidates from the pre-selector set.
🔵 [cursor-state-shared-file] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `<live>/runs-enrich-cursor.json` is read-modify-written by every `status runs` caller and every project watcher with tmp+rename but no lock (last writer wins); a loss needs one tick to span two others and only regresses the cursor, so rows are re-probed within ceil(live/cap) ticks. Excluded: fail-open and bounded; follow-up is merge-on-save or a watcher-private probe map.
🔵 [paths-file-wiped-on-git-failure] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `writePaths` overwrites `runs/paths/<key>.json` with `{}` when `git worktree list` fails or the watcher cwd is outside the repo (`scope.repo_identity` null), erasing the previous map until the next successful publish. Excluded: `set` launches with cwd=repo_root so the normal path is unaffected; follow-up is to skip the write on failure.
🔵 [foreground-launcher-signal-forwarding] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `launchUnderLock` waits in `spawnSync`; a SIGTERM sent to the outer node (e.g. `timeout`) is not forwarded, leaving the inner writer alive holding the lock (Ctrl-C hits the whole group and `--stop` still works). Excluded: `--stop` is the spec'd stop path; follow-up is signal forwarding in the foreground launcher.
🔵 [heartbeat-republishes-frozen-rows] CUT/FOLLOW-UP heartbeats republish `state.lastRuns`, so per-row `elapsed_s`/`probe_age_s`/`observed_at` can be minutes old while `counts` are recomputed every tick and freshness is judged by `published_at`, as the spec's fake-clock cases require. Excluded: matches the frozen acceptance; follow-up is to have readers derive elapsed from `started_at`/`fact_at` and note it in references.
🔵 [runs-live-schema-file] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `schemas/runs-live.schema.json` is listed in §3 under P1a but is not in this diff and not in rows R1–R5 (§3 is not a binding section). Excluded: not in the review rows; follow-up with the `validate-json-schema.js` gate in P1b.
🔵 [tmpdir-reported-as-flock-unavailable] CUT/FOLLOW-UP `flockAvailable` returns false when `os.tmpdir()` is unwritable, so the stderr line names `flock_unavailable` for a TMPDIR problem (pinned by session-mode-watcher.test.sh case 8). Excluded: exit code and one-line behaviour match the spec; follow-up is a distinct message for the mkdtemp failure.
